title: The big truck.
lines: And my daddy is a truck driver.
He drives a big red truck.
Because it's very big and very red.
Every day Daddy drives Red Giant along the roads.
To shops, to factories and to the harbour.
He takes things from one place to another.
I get to go with Daddy!
At six o'clock in the morning Daddy wakes me up.
I put on my clothes and my yellow cap.
Daddy gives me a sandwich and a cup of milk.
Then we go to the big car park where Red Giant is.
Wow, it's so big up close!
The wheels are bigger than me.
One, two, three, four, five, six.
There are lots and lots of wheels.
To get into the cab, I have to climb up some steps.
And behind the seats there's even a little bed, for sleeping when Daddy has to drive far.
I get a special seat, with a seat belt.
It shakes a little, like a big cat purring.
I can see over the cars.
The houses, the trees, the cows in the field.
First we drive to a big factory.
A man with a forklift loads boxes into the truck.
There are little bikes in them, and dolls, and blocks.
Daddy signs a piece of paper.
Trucks aren't allowed to go as fast as cars, Daddy tells me.
They need a lot of time to stop.
A blue one, a green one, one with a long tank full of milk.
Daddy has a button for the big horn.
A bird flies away in fright.
At twelve o'clock we stop at a car park.
We go into a little restaurant.
asks a woman in a red coat.
After lunch we drive to a big toy shop in the city.
The shop assistant gives me a truck sticker.
And do you know what I see in the shop?
A girl is looking at a pink bike.
Without trucks there would be nothing in the shops.
No toys, no clothes and no food.
In the afternoon we drive back home.
When I wake up, we're in the car park.
Daddy lifts me out of the cab.
Was it a good day, co-pilot?
Daddy, when I grow up I'll be a truck driver too.
You with Red Giant, and me with Little Giant.
Daddy laughs and gives me a hug.
